newsitem.title: GERMANY: German bank group says Bonn must cut back spending.
newsitem.headline: German bank group says Bonn must cut back spending.

text.p: Germany should find more places to cut spending, not raise taxes, to keep its budget deficit from increasing, a major German bank association said on Monday.
"In view of tax burdens that are already too high, a sensible consolidation can only come from the spending side," the Association of German Banks (BdB) said in a statement.

Increases in fuel and value-added taxes -- which the government and opposition Social Democrats have considered using to keep finances in balance -- "would be poison for the economic climate," BdB said.
Like other European nations, Germany must also reduce its deficit to meet the European monetary union deficit target of three percent of gross domestic product, the group noted.
The federal deficit in the first quarter was 40 billion marks, double the shortfall seen a year ago, BdB said.
The group cautioned, however, that the first quarter figures were affected by special factors and gave no reliable indication of revenues for the rest of the year.
"Additional vigorous consolidations measures are unavoidable" to keep public deficits from climbing even higher.
